items.titleZh: 芯片桥接神经形态与深度网络计算（德累斯顿工业大学）
items.descriptionZh:
由德国德累斯顿工业大学与英国曼彻斯特大学联合研究团队发表的技术论文《SpiNNaker2芯片：面向灵活可扩展类脑计算的多核平台》近日引发业界关注。该成果发表于半导体行业权威媒体Semiconductor Engineering，标志着类脑计算与深度学习两大技术路线之间正在出现实质性的融合节点。

**背景与上下文**

SpiNNaker系列芯片源自欧洲人脑计划（Human Brain Project），其核心理念是模拟生物神经网络的工作机制——通过大规模脉冲神经网络（Spiking Neural Network, SNN）实现事件驱动式计算。与传统的冯·诺依曼架构不同，SpiNNaker采用海量简单处理核心并行协作的方式，模仿大脑中神经元通过脉冲信号传递信息的模式。第一代SpiNNaker芯片于2011年问世，最初规划构建包含100万个ARM核的系统，但受限于功耗与制造工艺，实际规模与能效比均有提升空间。SpiNNaker2作为继承者，在架构设计上进行了根本性革新，其最突出的贡献在于：首次在硬件层面弥合了深度学习（深度神经网络）与神经形态计算之间的"鸿沟"。

**核心技术原理与创新**

SpiNNaker2的核心创新可归纳为三个层面。其一，"多核异构弹性计算"架构。芯片集成了数千个低功耗ARM处理器核心（Cortex-M系列架构），通过片上网络（Network-on-Chip）实现高带宽、低延迟的消息传递。与第一代相比，每个核心都增加了独立的动态电压与频率调节（DVFS）能力，这意味着不同核心可以根据任务负载实时调整功耗状态——类比生物大脑中神经元的兴奋与静息状态切换，能效较前代提升了一个数量级。

其二，"双重计算模式"融合。传统神经形态芯片（如IBM的TrueNorth）仅支持脉冲神经网络，而通用AI加速器（如GPU或NPU）侧重于连续数值的张量运算，两者互不兼容。SpiNNaker2在硬件层面同时支持两种模式：既能高效执行脉冲神经网络的稀疏、异步事件处理，也能完成传统深度网络所需的矩阵乘法与卷积运算。具体而言，芯片设计了可配置的乘累加单元，在脉冲模式下充当突触事件的积分器，在深度神经网络模式下则作为标准的MAC运算单元。这种双模设计允许开发者在一个平台上无缝切换或混用SNN与ANN模型。

其三，"片上学习"能力。SpiNNaker2内建了支持多种学习规则（包括脉冲时间依赖可塑性STDP、反向传播及在线梯度下降）的硬件逻辑，使芯片无需依赖外部主机即可完成模型训练与权重更新，这对于边缘场景中的持续学习至关重要。

**性能参数与对比分析**

论文报告了关键性能指标：在高性能模式下，SpiNNaker2可达到最高4.5 TOPS的算力。这一数字本身并非极致——相比之下，NVIDIA的嵌入式GPU Jetson Orin可提供约275 TOPS算力。但SpiNNaker2的价值不在于峰值算力的堆砌，而在于能效比与稀疏事件处理的效率。由于脉冲神经网络天然具备稀疏性和事件驱动特性，实际有效计算中无需像传统深度学习加速器那样激活所有乘法器；在典型SNN推理场景下，SpiNNaker2的每瓦特有效算力表现显著优于通用GPU方案。此外，芯片支持实时运行大规模脉冲神经网络仿真——这是GPU难以企及的——因为其片上通信网络严格设计为满足神经脉冲传播的时序要求，可对100万级神经元的网络进行实时模拟（相比第一代SpiNNaker的约10万级神经元，性能提升了约一个数量级）。多芯片可扩展性也是一大亮点：SpiNNaker2支持大规模互连，理论上可构建百亿神经元级别的超大规模系统，向全脑仿真目标迈进。

**技术影响与应用场景**

SpiNNaker2的出现对AI硬件生态具有多重意义。首先，它为研究社区提供了一个真正可编程的"类脑计算实验平台"——不同于功能固定的专用芯片，研究者可以在SpiNNaker2上试验新的神经元模型、连接拓扑和学习算法，这极大促进了计算神经科学的发展。其次，在产业应用层面，SpiNNaker2的"双模"能力使其成为边缘计算中兼顾深度神经网络与脉冲神经网络的理想选择：在功耗极度敏感的物联网设备、可穿戴健康监测终端中，SNN模式能以微瓦级功耗实现语音唤醒、异常事件检测；在需要更高精度的场景则切换至深度网络模式。机器人与无人机领域也受益明显：事件驱动的传感数据（如动态视觉传感器DVS输出）可直接与SNN计算对接，实现毫秒级响应。此外，德国德累斯顿工业大学与曼彻斯特大学联合组建的SpiNNcloud Systems公司已开始推进SpiNNaker2的商业化部署，拟构建以数千颗SpiNNaker2芯片组成的高密度计算集群，面向科研和工业用户提供类脑计算云服务。

总体而言，SpiNNaker2的突破在于证明了"神经形态"与"深度学习"这两个一度被视为此消彼长的技术方向可以在同一块硅片上共生共荣。它既是神经科学研究的先进工具，也为未来低功耗智能系统提供了全新的硬件基石。随着类脑芯片生态的逐步完善，我们有理由期待下一步将要出现的，是真正兼具大脑效率与深度学习能力的通用智能计算平台。

items.title: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
items.description: As AI systems outgrow copper interconnects, TSMC, Intel, Samsung Foundry, and GlobalFoundries are pursuing four distinctly different co-packaged optics strategies to bring optical connectivity closer to compute.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The requirements of AI clusters have made optical interconnections practical for scale-out connectivity, but as bandwidth requirements increase, optical connectivity is becoming viable for scale-up connections. As a result, the industry is moving optical interfaces closer to CPUs and GPUs, from the front-panel transceiver to the package itself through co-packaged optics (CPO), and eventually directly into the processor package.Optical connectivity has been used for decades, as electrical links cannot efficiently and reliably transmit data over long distances at high data transfer rates. However, the cost and complexity of optical components limited their use to long-reach connections.The importance of CPO is rising because electrical interconnects are no longer scaling as quickly as AI processors, and feeding thousands of accelerators within a data center requires an exponential increase in communication bandwidth. In a traditional optical networking architecture, the processor or switch ASIC communicates electrically with a pluggable optical transceiver located at the front panel of a server or switch. However, as signaling speeds climb to 200 Gb/s - 400 Gb/s per lane and beyond, transmitting electrical signals over long copper PCB traces on a motherboard becomes increasingly inefficient due to higher insertion loss, greater power consumption, and tighter signal integrity requirements.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While technically possible, it demands the use of better materials, retimers, complex compensation processing, and equalization circuitry, which increases the cost of server infrastructure and its power consumption. CPO moves optical engines next to the processor or switch ASIC to shorten the electrical path before signals are converted into light, which means lower power consumption per transmitted bit, increased bandwidth density, and predictable scalability. As a result, CPO is increasingly viewed as a necessary technology for next-generation AI infrastructure.Because AI is viewed as a major megatrend, CPO is set to become ubiquitous; there are dozens of companies working in the CPO ecosystem, including foundries, OSATs, optical I/O startups, laser manufacturers, fiber suppliers, packaging houses, and networking vendors. You may like Inside optical and the battle for scale Leading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel and Samsung — outlining the path to 1.4nm nodes and beyond Intel's EMIB packaging gains traction as chip designers look beyond TSMC's constrained CoWoS As there are so many vendors pursuing different goals with different strategies, for this story, we are going to limit ourselves only to companies that actually produce things and whose roadmaps reflect their technological capabilities. So far, only four foundries have publicly articulated meaningful CPO manufacturing strategies: Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries, Samsung Foundry, and TSMC.The four companies each represent four different CPO strategies and have very distinct plans for the future, so their plans and capabilities may not be directly comparable. Nonetheless, reviewing their offerings gives us an idea about where the industry is going from the perspective of actual foundries.TSMC: COUPE for everythingTSMC has historically been absent from the optical connectivity market as a product supplier. However, having worked on silicon photonics for many years, it now has the broadest ecosystem and manufacturing roadmap with its Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE). (Image credit: TSMC)TSMC's silicon photonics technology roadmap currently has three stages that span from a 1.6 Tbps optical engine with conventional pluggable optics to a 12.8 Tbps optical engine located within a processor package. The COUPE roadmap is tightly coupled with the company's advanced packaging technologies and the evolution of the company's micro-ring modulators (MRMs) that modulate light and directly impact performance. As a result, several TSMC customers (e.g., Nvidia) plot their silicon photonics strategies around the evolution of COUPE.The first phase of the roadmap — called COUPE on PCB — relies on a COUPE that bonds a 65nm electronic integrated circuit (EIC) with a photonic integrated circuit (PIC) using the company's SoIC-X bonding technology. The initial implementation targets OSFP (Octal Small Form-factor Pluggable) optical modules and delivers 1.6 Tbps of bandwidth (2x the throughput of copper Ethernet solutions, along with 2x the power efficiency compared to copper). Therefore, the first-gen COUPE is out of the scope of this article. TSMC says the SoIC-X interface features very low impedance and enables lower power consumption at high signaling speeds. What to read next Trailing-edge foundry roadmaps for GlobalFoundries, UMC, and SMIC The custom AI ASIC state of play (May 2026) — Broadcom deals, Google TPUs, Meta MTIA & beyond Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecks The second generation — dubbed COUPE on substrate — marks TSMC's transition from conventional pluggable optics to co-packaged optics (CPO). In this stage, COUPE is integrated with the company's chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging technology and co-packaged with a network switch ASIC. This architecture enables motherboard-level optical interconnects with aggregate bandwidth up to 6.4 Tbps, 2x power efficiency, and 10x lower latency compared to existing pluggable solutions, which is fantastic for a variety of applications, such as NVLink, Ethernet, and InfiniBand switches.The third phase — called COUPE on interposer — pushes silicon photonics even closer to compute dies: a 12.8 Tbps optical engine is integrated directly into the processor package to enable ultimate bandwidth and scalability. Beyond doubling bandwidth again, the company expects the architecture to offer 5x power efficiency and 20x lower latency compared to pluggable solutions used today. That will make it particularly attractive for use by hyperscalers that build clusters consisting of thousands of accelerators. Unfortunately, TSMC characterizes this phase as exploratory and has not disclosed its commercialization timeline. Swipe to scroll horizontally TSMC COUPE's MRM Evolution Year 2026 2028 2029 2030 MRM / Lane Speed 200 Gb/s 200 Gb/s 200 Gb/s 400 Gb/s Bandwidth Density 0.5 Tbps/mm 1 Tbps/mm 2 Tbps/mm 4 Tbps/mm Wavelenght Single Single Multi Multi FAU Single-row FAU Dual-rou FAU Dual-rou FAU Dual-rou FAU The main agenda of COUPE is to move the optical engine as close to compute as possible. However, there is another dimension in TSMC's silicon photonics strategy: the evolution of the photonic devices themselves, the MRMs integrated into PICs. The company plans to bring the world's first 200 Gbps/lane (wavelength) micro-ring modulator into production in 2026 and then continue scaling the technology with 400 Gb/s MRMs, additional optical wavelengths, and denser fiber-array integration. This evolution is expected to increase COUPE’s bandwidth density from 0.5 Tb/s/mm in 2026 to 4 Tb/s/mm by 2030, providing an 8x improvement over four years.It is noteworthy that TSMC presents the MRM roadmap separately from the evolution of COUPE packaging, which suggests that advances in micro-ring modulators represent an independent technology roadmap for the photonic integrated circuit (PIC), rather than being tied to a specific packaging generation. This potentially means that future COUPE products could adopt newer generations of MRMs regardless of whether the optical engine is mounted on a PCB, package substrate, or silicon interposer, although the latter will probably deliver the greatest system-level benefits by minimizing the electrical distance between compute dies and optical interfaces.Intel: Optics for CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, and acceleratorsIntel has been shipping various products with optical interconnections for decades and even attached its silicon photonics solutions to Xeon and Xeon Phi processors in the mid-2010s. Today, Intel's public CPO roadmap is less explicit than TSMC's, but its direction is fairly clear: move optical I/O directly next to CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, and eventually other compute chiplets. Meanwhile, so far, Intel has not unveiled plans to use its CPO technology for switches. (Image credit: Intel)Intel's CPO strategy is largely focused on its Optical Compute Interconnect (OCI) chiplet, which is a self-contained optical I/O subsystem packing both EIC and PIC that can be co-packaged with any compute device using a PCIe interface to enable high-performance optical connectivity. Intel demonstrated the first OCI in 2024. That prototype implementation used 64 PCIe 5.0 lanes at 32 GT/s in each direction to connect to the host and provided 4 Tbps of bidirectional optical bandwidth over eight fiber pairs over a distance of up to 100 meters. Each fiber carried eight DWDM wavelengths spaced at 200 GHz, and every wavelength (lane) transported about 32 Gbps (8 FPs × 8 WLs × 32 Gbps = 2,048 Gbps in each direction). (Image credit: Intel)The 2024 OCI implementation is good for testing the technology, but with rather slow 32 Gbps lanes, it has not been adopted commercially. Meanwhile, this technology has already been proven and demonstrated. Intel is currently working on its next-generation OCI with 200G/lane PICs to support 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps applications, though it is unclear when it is set to be available, as Intel has not yet disclosed an equivalent to TSMC's MRM roadmap.It should be noted that future OCI implementations supporting bandwidth of 10s of terabits per second could interface with compute dies using next-generation PCIe 6.0 interfaces or even native die-to-die UCIe links when integrated into commercial products. Furthermore, Intel can naturally integrate OCI chiplets using its advanced packaging technologies to ensure high performance and low power. (Image credit: Intel)As noted above, Intel's focus with OCI has always been its integration with CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, accelerators, or other compute devices, but not necessarily switches. It remains to be seen whether Intel's next-generation AI hardware roadmap will include switching silicon, but for now, it does not seem that the company is targeting optical switches with its OCI chiplets. Since OCI is protocol-agnostic, limiting it to compute devices seems like an artificial limitation, though we have little indication about Intel's reasoning behind the decision.Samsung Foundry: Addressing everythingSamsung Foundry's silicon photonics strategy is arguably the most comprehensive among leading foundries. Unlike Intel, whose CPO roadmap is focused on its OCI chiplet for integration with compute devices, or TSMC, whose COUPE optical engine is another major ingredient of its foundry platform, Samsung intends to offer all types of optical connectivity devices, starting from pluggable transceivers in 2026, to switch CPO later on, and all the way to optical engines on the interposer of a processor package in 2030. Unfortunately, Samsung does not publicly provide a lot of information about its plans, so our main source of information will be SF's slide from a conference published by SemiVision. (Image credit: SemiVision)This year, Samsung Foundry intends to offer a merchant PIC platform that relies on an EIC and a PIC mounted side by side on a PCB for conventional pluggable optics. The PIC will support 100 Gbps-class optical interfaces using CWDM technology, which is good enough for traditional pluggable optical transceivers (though Samsung does not specify the exact implementation), so there's no indication of CPO here. (Image credit: Samsung)In 2027, Samsung Foundry intends to catch up with TSMC's first-gen COUPE and offer an optical engine that stacks an EIC on top of a PIC using thermo-compression bonding (TCB). Samsung expects energy efficiency of this generation to improve from approximately 10 pJ/bit for its initial PIC platform to 5 pJ/bit, though Samsung has said nothing about bandwidth or latency. Samsung's TCB-based OE seems to be an intermediate product between merchant PICs and true CPO, so it will generally address onboard optics and pluggable transceivers.By 2028, SF intends to move optical engines to the substrate of Ethernet or InfiniBand switch ASICs, which will be its first true CPO. The company intends to adopt hybrid copper bonding (HCB) with 10 µm pitches for its OEs to improve bandwidth density. Based on the slide from the roadmap, to address next-generation switches, Samsung is poised to increase optical lane speeds from 100 Gbps to 200 Gbps and ultimately 400 Gbps, although the company does not disclose when exactly each speed bin will be introduced (though it looks like 400 Gbps will come in 2029 – 2030) as well as the underlying modulator technology or other device-level details behind this scaling.In 2029, Samsung Foundry will finally integrate its optical engine on an interposer next to CPU/GPU/XPU or other compute device, which will reduce energy consumption to 2 pJ/bit while providing extremely high bandwidth. Samsung calls this 'CPO Turnkey,' which implies that such integration will require its own packaging technologies. The next step in Samsung's roadmap is called 'next-generation CPO Turnkey,' and it integrates virtually the entire optical subsystem — including lasers — alongside compute and memory, which will be its ultimate CPO offering expected by 2030 and onwards.While Samsung Foundry's ultimate goal to offer highly integrated turnkey CPO solutions is clear, the company also intends to offer two merchant platforms for pluggable optical transceivers, perhaps to de-risk development of its future products and to capitalize on the high demand for optical connectivity that exists today and will continue going forward.GlobalFoundries: A bespoke vendor-agnostic OCI-MSA CPO platformUnlike Intel Foundry, Samsung Foundry, and TSMC, GlobalFoundries does not produce or intend to produce AI processors, switch ASICs, or advanced packages. Instead, it aims to become a merchant co-packaged optics provider that will produce and sell bespoke CPO solutions that enable optical connectivity (including OCI MSA connectivity) for processors made by other chipmakers. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)GF's silicon photonics effort dates back to the IBM Microelectronics acquisition in 2015, which brought IBM's silicon photonics technology and engineering teams into the company. Over the years, GlobalFoundries has expanded its silicon photonics capabilities into what eventually became the GF Fotonix platform and, more recently, the company acquired AMF and InfiniLink to further strengthen its production and design capabilities.The key element of GlobalFoundries' CPO strategy is its Silicon photonics Co-packaged Advanced Light Engine (SCALE) platform that combines photonic IP, advanced packaging technologies, and a reference optical engine architecture that includes EIC and PIC. Unlike Intel's OCI chiplet, SCALE allows GF's clients to customize optical engines in accordance with their needs and have them manufactured by GF.Under the program, GlobalFoundries manufactures the PIC and EIC using its own process technologies and then packages them into an OCI MSA-compliant optical engine using its methods. If the EIC requires a leading-edge node that GF does not have, it could instead be fabricated by another foundry and then integrated by GF. Customers then co-package the optical engine alongside their own switch ASICs or AI accelerators.For now, SCALE supports both CWDM and DWDM transmission using qualified 50 Gbps and 100 Gbps MRMs, integrated photodiodes, and coupled-ring resonators. The platform has demonstrated bidirectional operation with up to 16 DWDM lanes per fiber, which theoretically opens doors to optical links with up to 1.6 Tb/s of bandwidth per direction. On the integration side of things, it supports advanced 2.5D and 3D integration using TSVs and copper bonding with pitches ranging from 110 µm to below 45 µm, which is good enough for integration using CoWoS-S and CoWoS-L technologies.Just like Intel with its OCI, GlobalFoundries does not necessarily tie its SCALE CPO customers to its silicon or packaging technologies. Furthermore, the company allows its clients to customize their optical engines while retaining compatibility with the OCI-MSA requirements.The future of CPO Co-packaged optics (CPO) is set to become a key technology for next-generation AI infrastructure as conventional electrical interconnects struggle to keep pace with the bandwidth demands of rapidly developing AI processors.Among foundries, TSMC, Intel, Samsung Foundry, and GlobalFoundries have each developed distinct CPO strategies that range from merchant optical engines to optical I/O chiplets and vertically integrated CPO platforms.Given the different capabilities of the contract chipmakers, their roadmaps differ significantly in both scope and implementation, with some companies trying to lock in customers with a proprietary platform and others offering different degrees of freedom.However, they all share the same objective: move optical interfaces progressively closer to compute dies to reduce power consumption, increase bandwidth density, and lower latency for the next generation of AI systems that will require considerably more bandwidth than today's clusters.

items.titleZh: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
items.descriptionZh:
随着AI集群规模不断扩大，传统电互连已难以满足海量加速器之间爆炸式增长的通信带宽需求。虽然光互连已在长距离传输中应用数十年，但过去由于成本和复杂度较高，仅用于远距离连接。如今，光互连正从服务器前面板的可插拔光模块向芯片封装内部迁移，即“共封装光学”（Co-Packaged Optics, CPO）技术——将光引擎移至处理器或交换ASIC的旁边，在信号转换为光之前大幅缩短电学传输路径。这样做不仅能降低每比特传输功耗，还能提高带宽密度并实现可预测的扩展性，因此被视为下一代AI基础设施的关键技术。

在CPO生态系统中，目前只有四家晶圆代工厂公开了明确的制造路线图：台积电、英特尔、三星代工和格芯（GlobalFoundries）。它们各自代表四种不同的技术路径，未来发展策略与能力各具特色。

**台积电：COUPE路线图**

台积电通过其“紧凑型通用光子引擎”（COUPE）平台制定了三阶段硅光发展计划，并与自有先进封装技术和微环调制器（MRM）的演进深度绑定。第一阶段“COUPE on PCB”采用65nm电子IC（EIC）与光子IC（PIC）通过SoIC-X键合技术堆叠，用于OSFP光模块，提供1.6Tbps带宽，功率效率为铜缆的两倍，但不属于CPO范畴。第二阶段“COUPE on substrate”标志着向共封装光学过渡，光引擎集成到CoWoS先进封装中，与网络交换ASIC共封装，可实现6.4Tbps聚合带宽、2倍功率效率以及相比可插拔方案低10倍的延迟，适用于NVLink、以太网和InfiniBand交换机。第三阶段“COUPE on interposer”则是直接把12.8Tbps光引擎集成进处理器封装内，预期可提供5倍功率效率和20倍延迟改善，非常适合构建数千个加速器的超大规模集群，但该阶段目前仍处于探索期，商业化时间未定。

台积电另一条独立的技术演进路线是微环调制器。公司计划在2026年推出业界首个200Gbps/波长的微环调制器，后续进一步提升至400Gb/s，并引入多波长支持和更密集的光纤阵列。这将使COUPE的带宽密度从2026年的0.5Tbps/mm提升至2030年的4Tbps/mm，四年内提升8倍。值得注意的是，MRM路线图与COUPE封装阶段分开演进，意味着未来无论光引擎位于PCB、基板还是硅中介层上，都可以采用更新的调制器技术，从而获得系统级性能提升。

**英特尔：面向计算设备的光学互连小芯片**

英特尔长期深耕光互连产品，早在2010年代中期就将硅光方案与Xeon处理器结合。其CPO战略的核心是“光学计算互连”（OCI）小芯片——一个完整的、同时包含EIC和PIC的光I/O子系统，可通过PCIe接口与任意计算设备共封装。2024年展示的OCI原型采用双向各64条PCIe 5.0通道（每通道32GT/s），通过8对光纤提供4Tbps双向光带宽，每根光纤承载8个间隔200GHz的DWDM波长，每个波长速率约32Gbps，传输距离达100米。不过该原型通道速率偏低（32Gbps），尚未商业化。目前英特尔正在开发采用200G/通道PIC的下一代OCI，支持800Gbps和1.6Tbps应用，但时间表未公布。未来OCI有望通过PCIe 6.0或UCIe原生芯粒互连接口与计算die连接，支持数十Tbps级别带宽。与台积电不同，英特尔当前OCI定位明确指向CPU、GPU、DPU和加速器，而非交换芯片；由于OCI协议无关，这一限制更多是策略选择而非技术必然。

**三星代工：从可插拔到Turnkey全覆盖**

三星代工的硅光路线图在前沿代工厂中覆盖最广，从2026年的可插拔方案逐步走向2030年的高度集成封装。2026年，三星计划提供采用EIC和PIC并列放置在PCB上的商用PIC平台，支持100Gbps级CWDM光接口，应用于传统可插拔光模块。2027年，采用热压键合（TCB）将EIC堆叠在PIC上方，能效从约10pJ/bit提升至5pJ/bit，这属于板载光学而非真正的CPO。到2028年，三星将把光引擎转移至以太网或InfiniBand交换ASIC的封装基板上，这是其第一款真正意义上的CPO产品，采用混合铜键合（HCB）技术，间距10微米，通道速率计划从100Gbps逐步提升至400Gbps（后者预计在2029至2030年之间）。2029年，光引擎将集成到中介层上，与CPU/GPU/XPU相邻，能效降至2pJ/bit，带宽极高，三星称其为“CPO Turnkey”。而2030年及以后的“下一代CPO Turnkey”将把包括激光器在内的几乎整个光学子系统与计算和内存一同封装，达到终极集成度。此外，三星还会提供两个商用可插拔方案平台，既为了增加收入，也为了降低未来CPO开发风险。

**GlobalFoundries：定制化、厂商中立的SCALE平台**

与前三家不同，格芯不生产AI处理器或交换ASIC，而是定位为独立CPO供应商，为其他芯片厂商制造定制光引擎。其硅光技术源自2015年收购IBM微电子业务，经过多年扩展形成GF Fotonix平台，近期又并购了AMF和InfiniLink以强化设计与生产。格芯CPO战略的核心是“SCALE”平台（Silicon photonics Co-packaged Advanced Light Engine），整合了光子IP、先进封装技术和包含EIC/PIC的参考光引擎架构。客户可根据需求定制光引擎，并交由格芯制造；即使客户需要更先进的EIC节点，格芯也可将其外包给其他代工厂再集成。SCALE平台目前支持CWDM和DWDM传输，采用经过验证的50Gbps/100Gbps微环调制器、集成光电探测器和耦合环形谐振器，已演示在单根光纤上支持多达16个DWDM波长，理论可实现每方向最高1.6Tbps光链路。集成方面支持TSV和铜键合，间距从110微米到低于45微米，可兼容CoWoS-S和CoWoS-L等封装技术。同时格芯不强制绑定自有硅工艺或封装路线，允许客户在符合OCI MSA标准的前提下灵活定制。

总的来看，CPO正在成为下一代AI基础设施不可或缺的支撑技术。台积电、英特尔、三星代工和格芯虽路径各异——有的以专有平台锁定客户，有的提供更大自由度——但目标一致：将光学接口不断推向计算die附近，以降低功耗、提升带宽密度并减少延迟，满足未来AI系统远高于当前集群的通信要求。

items.title: GPU prices keep surging in 2026 — Lack of sale discounts and rising VRAM costs keep current-gen prices sky-high
items.description: AI, tariffs, and greed have put pressure on PC builders wanting a new GPU. Can you still get a cheap GPU?
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter We all know the current state of pricing for PC components is through the roof. Looking back, we have the hindsight to see what the prices were a year or two ago, and be thankful that we bought something when it was cheaper or on a really good sale. But for those who didn’t upgrade back then, what does the future look like if you want to upgrade your graphics card?Currently, we have access to the 50-series range of graphics cards from Nvidia, and the 90-series from AMD, with a couple of entries from Intel. These cards were primarily released in January 2025, with different graphics card SKUs released throughout the year. We’re now more than halfway through 2026, with the rumored release of the next generation of graphics cards not arriving until late 2027, or even 2028, so we’re looking at at least a year before we see any hint of a new GPU release.Why the delay or extended release cadence? Well, the simple answer is the costs. Just one aspect of the increased costs incurred with any new graphics card release will be the high-speed memory used, and, in the GPU's case, the amount of VRAM. Prices have become exponentially more expensive due to the AI crunch, so adding more memory to a GPU is going to not only increase the production costs of any new graphics card direct from Nvidia or AMD, but also boost the expenses that AIB board partners have to incur to offer the partner GPUs. These manufacturing cost rises will, of course, be passed on to us poor consumers. There might even be reductions in the amount of onboard VRAM for different card SKUs; we will have to wait to find out.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: There are no stock issues with picking up a new GPU; the main issue is just the cost. I keep track of all the current graphics card prices twice weekly in our GPU Price Index, and have seen the prices creep up steadily since release, especially with the higher-end and more popular GPUs, or those deemed the best performance per dollar.Here are two tables that show the initial MSRP launch prices of Nvidia’s 50-series and AMD’s 90-series graphics cards, along with the current price and the lowest prices that we’ve seen for each card. This generation of cards was released with a higher MSRP, and many GPUs released were well above the announced MSRP prices set by Nvidia and AMD, garnering a lot of criticism from both the press and consumers. What’s also been highly noticeable this generation is the lack of notable below-MSRP discounts in major sales events such as Black Friday or Prime Day. With cards such as Nvidia’s flagship GeForce RTX 5090 never dropping below its initial release price. In the case of the RTX 5090, the price of the top-tier GPU that features 32GB of precious VRAM has only ever increased, rising from $1,999 to $4,288, a staggering $2,289 (114.5%) difference.As I see the cheapest models sell out while I’m checking on the weekly prices, the cost of the GPU just keeps climbing a little higher every time. Although the RTX 5090 is the most extreme example of GPU inflation, it is unfortunately not alone.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)AMD’s Radeon RX 9070 XT, which many feel to be the value champion for high-end GPUs, competes against Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti, but for several hundred dollars less. Up until very recently, the 9070 XT held a steady $699 retail price, but as of writing, the price has jumped to $719, a $120 hike from the $599 launch MSRP price, a 20% increase. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)To help in your decision of what card you want to buy, consider what features the card offers and what you will make use of. Is ray-tracing important to you? Does frame gen technology interest you? Are the video encoders and codecs for streaming or video capture better for your associated software? Do your research; don’t just look at graphs with FPS numbers. Think about what is going to give you the most overall benefit.Other things to also consider are the differences in the supporting software, such as FSR and DLSS, with Nvidia slightly ahead for the most part for the latest technology, but with the caveat that they are also more expensive. AMD cards this generation have offered more VRAM on lower-end GPU SKUs, which can be an important feature for gamers playing on higher-resolution monitors with game settings dialed up.If you want a graphics card now, you don’t have much choice but to grab what you can at the lowest price that’s available to you at the moment. Holding out for the next generation of GPUs often isn’t going to save you any money; as with all technology, obsolescence is a fact of life.We have to wait for the definitive specifications to be announced for the new GPU lineups, and until then, everything is educated guesswork and speculation. Whether reductions in onboard VRAM allocations take place, GPU die size shrinks, or core counts multiply, all wait to be seen. Whatever happens, though, one thing is guaranteed, and that is that the new lineup will be more expensive than this generation; we just don’t know yet by how much.Finding a massive discount on a graphics card in the current economic climate is going to be limited to stores making pricing mistakes or some serious combo bundle deals from retailers. Seeing how even the Nvidia 40-series and AMD 70-series GPUs have held value and not greatly depreciated is an indication that the current generation of cards is not going to see massive discounts closer to the launch of the next generation. We hold out hope that we may see some discounts in the next Black Friday sales, but I wouldn’t count on seeing anything truly jaw-dropping, although I do hope to be proven wrong.
items.author: Stewart Bendle
items.titleZh: GPU价格在2026年持续飙升——缺乏促销折扣和显存成本上涨使当前世代价格居高不下
items.descriptionZh:
PC显卡市场正经历前所未有的价格暴涨，这已成为当前硬件领域最受关注的话题。回顾一两年前的价格，如今再想升级显卡的消费者无疑会感到沉重的经济压力。目前市场上可供选择的主要是英伟达（Nvidia）的RTX 50系列和AMD的RX 90系列显卡，另有英特尔（Intel）的几款产品，这些显卡大多在2025年1月发布，不同型号在此后陆续上市。然而，当前时间已进入2026年年中，下一代显卡据传要到2027年底甚至2028年才会亮相，这意味着玩家至少还要等待一年以上才有可能看到新GPU的影子。

这一漫长的产品周期背后，核心原因归结为一个字：成本。任何新显卡的推出都伴随着高昂的制造成本，而其中最具代表性的便是高速显存（VRAM）的支出。由于人工智能（AI）热潮引发的算力竞赛，显存颗粒的价格呈指数级上涨。这意味着无论是英伟达还是AMD直接推出的公版显卡，还是AIB合作伙伴（如华硕、微星、技嘉等）推出的非公版产品，其生产成本都将大幅抬升——更多的显存意味着更高的物料成本，而这些最终都会转嫁给消费者。更令人担忧的是，为了控制成本，未来不同型号的显卡甚至可能在板载显存容量上做出缩减，具体细节仍需拭目以待。

与往年不同，目前购买新显卡已不存在缺货问题，真正的障碍纯粹是价格。Tom's Hardware的GPU价格指数追踪显示，自发布以来，各款显卡的价格持续稳步攀升，尤其是高端型号和性价比口碑较好的热门产品。从两张价格对比表中可以清晰看到这一趋势的严峻程度。英伟达RTX 50系列方面，旗舰RTX 5090的官方建议零售价（MSRP）为1,999美元，历史最低价也从未跌破此价位，但当前最佳购买价已飙升至4,288美元，涨幅高达2,289美元，即114.5%。RTX 5080从999美元的MSRP涨至1,256美元，最低曾降至929美元；RTX 5070 Ti从749美元涨至949美元；RTX 5070从549美元涨至629美元；RTX 5060 Ti 16GB从429美元涨至569美元；RTX 5060 Ti 8GB从379美元涨至429美元；RTX 5060从299美元涨至339美元；RTX 5050从249美元涨至289美元。AMD RX 90系列同样不容乐观，被许多玩家视为高端性价比之王的RX 9070 XT，MSRP为599美元，此前一直稳定在699美元零售价，而截至本文撰写时已跳涨至719美元，较首发价高出120美元，涨幅达20%。RX 9070从549美元涨至639美元；RX 9060 XT 16GB从349美元涨至449美元；RX 9060 XT 8GB从299美元涨至359美元。

纵观整体数据，各款显卡的历史最低价几乎都难以跌破首发MSRP，甚至许多型号从未低于发布价格。这一代显卡在发布之初就定下了较高的MSRP，而实际上市价格更是普遍远超官方定价，引发了媒体和消费者的广泛批评。尤为值得注意的是，即便是黑色星期五或Prime Day这类传统的大型促销活动，也鲜见低于MSRP的大幅折扣——这在过去几代产品中几乎不可想象。

RTX 5090作为搭载32GB珍贵显存的顶级旗舰，是GPU通胀最极端的案例，但绝非孤例。从作者追踪每周价格的经历来看，最便宜的型号总是迅速售罄，而剩余显卡的价格则每次都在小幅攀升。这种"越等越贵"的态势让持币观望的消费者陷入两难。

在选购建议方面，专家提醒消费者不应仅仅盯着帧率（FPS）数字对比图，而应综合考虑显卡的实际功能特性：光线追踪性能是否符合你的需求？帧生成技术（Frame Generation）是否吸引你？视频编码器和编解码器是否更适合你使用的流媒体或录制软件？同时，配套软件生态的差异也值得关注——AMD的FSR与Nvidia的DLSS各有优劣，英伟达在最新技术上总体略微领先，但价格也更高昂；AMD这一代在中低端型号上提供了更大的显存容量，这对于在高分辨率显示器上开启高画质设置的玩家来说是一个重要考量因素。

对于当下需要升级显卡的消费者，现实的选择并不多：只能以当前能找到的最低价格尽快入手。等待下一代产品往往并不能省钱——正如所有科技产品一样，迭代与淘汰是不可避免的宿命。在下一代GPU的最终规格公布之前，一切关于显存容量调整、芯片制程缩减或核心数量增加的说法都只是基于现有信息的合理推测。但有一件事是确定的：下一代显卡阵容必将比当前这一代更加昂贵，只是我们尚不清楚贵多少而已。

在当前的经济环境下，想要找到大幅折扣的显卡，恐怕只能寄望于零售商的定价失误或罕见的捆绑促销套餐。一个值得注意的信号是，就连英伟达40系列和AMD 70系列的上一代产品至今仍保持着较好的保值率，没有出现大幅贬值，这表明当前这一代显卡在下一代发布前夕也不太可能迎来大规模降价。作者表示，尽管希望在下一个黑色星期五能看到一些真正令人心动的优惠，但从目前的市场态势来看，恐怕不宜抱有过高的期待。

items.content: Chinese tech giant Alibaba released what it says is its largest and “most capable AI model to date,” claiming performance rivaling the best systems from US frontier labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as domestic rivals like Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3. Alibaba said it was making the model, Qwen3.8-Max, widely available to users in a blog post published on Monday. The release had been expected after the company previewed the model last month, when it claimed it was “second only to Fable 5,” Anthropic’s flagship.The open release of another highly capable Chinese AI model adds to sky-high tensions along multiple fronts in Silicon Valley and Washington over how to safely manage AI systems and retain the US’ technological edge over China.Results from Alibaba’s own testing shared on Monday suggests it’s as powerful as claimed, as does its ranking on crowdsourced model-comparison platform Arena.AI. Alibaba’s own testing shows the model’s performance to broadly match — and sometimes exceed — that of Fable 5 on benchmark tests. On the Arena text model leaderboard, Qwen3.8-Max trails only Fable 5 and three models in Anthropic’s Opus family. For frontend coding, it is beaten only by two Claude Opus models and Kimi K3, and for visual analysis, only Fable 5 trounces it.Alibaba says Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4 trillion parameters, a numerical measure of the settings a model learns during training that it uses to process data, recognize patterns, and undertake various tasks. While parameter counts are widely used as a shorthand for model performance, a bigger number does not always mean better. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 model has 2.8 trillion parameters, but most top American labs keep figures private, and neither OpenAI nor Anthropic disclose exact counts for their top systems.The Chinese company said it will release the weights for Qwen3.8-Max next week. Weights are the adjustable numerical values of an AI that determine how it processes information. Open-weight systems, while more restrictive than traditional open-source software, give developers far more control than they have over proprietary products from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Qwen3.8-Max marks a return to open-weight releases for Alibaba after the company briefly pivoted towards proprietary releases for its more advanced models earlier this year.Open-weight releases have become a growing point of differentiation for China’s AI industry, where they have become the norm. Moonshot released Kimi K3’s last week and many other top AI models are also open-weight. Beijing has championed the strategy as a means of growing China’s influence in global AI governance and encouraging widespread adoption of domestic tech champions.Alibaba’s release intensifies competition with China, whose firms appear to be rapidly narrowing the gap with US companies and have increased the tempo of releases in recent weeks. Qwen3.8-Max closely follows the release of Kimi K3, viewed as another challenge to American AI dominance, and both ByteDance and MiniMax released capable new video generation models on Friday.Openness has also proved to be a divisive issue. Amid reports of potential crackdown on open tools in the wake of the Chinese releases, the US industry has largely rallied around preserving access to open-weight models, both as a safety necessity and as means of preserving competition. That debate comes as closed-model providers, notably OpenAI and Anthropic, face increasing scrutiny after revealing a slew of cyberattacks unknowingly perpetrated by their own escaped AI agents. Incident reports from one victim suggest the restrictive safety rails intended to stop nefarious use of AI models also limits their use as defensive tools.

items.titleZh: 中国阿里巴巴再次挑战美国AI霸主地位
items.descriptionZh:
阿里巴巴于本周一正式发布了其迄今为止规模最大、号称“能力最强”的AI模型Qwen3.8-Max，并宣布向用户广泛开放。该公司在一篇博客文章中表示，该模型的性能足以媲美美国前沿实验室Anthropic和OpenAI的顶级系统，以及国内竞争对手月之暗面（Moonshot AI）的Kimi K3。此前在上个月的预告中，阿里巴巴曾声称该模型“仅次于Anthropic的旗舰产品Fable 5”，本次发布可谓在预期之内。

Qwen3.8-Max的开放发布，再度加剧了硅谷与华盛顿在多个维度的高度紧张——既涉及如何安全管理AI系统，也关乎美国能否维持对华技术优势。据阿里巴巴周一公布的内部测试结果，该模型实力确如其宣称，在众包模型对比平台Arena.AI上的排名也印证了这一点。自家评测显示，在基准测试中Qwen3.8-Max的表现总体上与Fable 5持平，部分项目甚至有所超越。在Arena文本模型排行榜上，Qwen3.8-Max仅次于Fable 5及Anthropic Opus系列中的三款模型；在前端编码任务中，仅落后于两款Claude Opus模型和Kimi K3；在视觉分析任务中，只有Fable 5能胜过它。

阿里巴巴表示，Qwen3.8-Max拥有2.4万亿参数。参数是衡量模型在训练中习得的“设置”数量的数值指标，用于处理数据、识别模式和执行各类任务。尽管参数数量常被当作模型性能的粗略指标，但更大的数字并不必然意味着更强。月之暗面的Kimi K3参数规模达2.8万亿，而大多数美国顶尖实验室对具体数字讳莫如深，OpenAI和Anthropic均未披露其顶级旗舰模型的准确参数。

这家中国科技巨头还透露，将于下周发布Qwen3.8-Max的权重。权重是决定AI如何处理信息的可调数值，开放权重系统虽比传统开源软件更具限制性，却能让开发者获得远超OpenAI、Anthropic等闭源产品的控制力。值得注意的是，Qwen3.8-Max标志着阿里巴巴在短暂转向专有发布策略后，重新回归开放权重路线。今年早些时候，该公司曾对其更先进的模型采用闭源方式。

开放权重正日益成为中国AI产业的差异化优势，并已成为行业常态。月之暗面上周已发布Kimi K3，许多其他顶尖中国AI模型同样开放权重。北京方面积极倡导这一策略，以此扩大中国在全球AI治理中的影响力，并推动本土科技领军企业获得更广泛的应用。阿里巴巴此次发布进一步加剧了竞争——中国公司正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，并明显加快发布节奏。Qwen3.8-Max紧随Kimi K3之后问世，后者同样被视为对美国AI主导地位的一次挑战；此外，字节跳动和MiniMax也于上周五发布了功能强大的新一代视频生成模型。

开放性本身也已成为一个颇具争议的话题。在中国密集发布开放权重模型后，美国有报道称可能对开放工具采取限制措施，但美国业界大体上一致支持保留开放权重模型的访问权，这既是出于安全必要，也是维持竞争的手段。与此形成对照的是，闭源模型提供商（尤其是OpenAI和Anthropic）正面临越来越严格的审视，原因是它们披露了一系列由自身失控AI代理无意中实施的网络攻击。来自某受害者的事件报告表明，旨在阻止AI模型被恶意使用的严格安全护栏，反而限制了这些模型作为防御工具的效能。

总体而言，Qwen3.8-Max的发布是中国AI能力持续跃升的标志性事件。凭借其媲美美国顶尖闭源模型的基准表现、庞大参数规模以及开放权重策略，它既为全球开发者提供了强大的开源替代方案，也在前沿编码、视觉分析等垂直场景中展现出直接应用潜力。与此同时，围绕开放与封闭、安全与竞争的全球博弈，正随着此类模型的不断涌现而愈发激烈。

items.content: Fender CEO Edward “Bud” Cole gave an interview to T3 in May celebrating the 75th anniversary of the Telecaster with comments on AI and music that initially flew under the radar. But it has started making the rounds recently, pouring more fuel on an already raging fire of bad PR following the company pissing off basically the entire guitar-playing community by sending cease-and-desist letters to builders, claiming copyright of the Stratocaster body shape.Some influential guitar YouTubers have even said they’re done buying Fender gear in the wake of the controversy. And Cole’s resurfaced comments comparing cover songs and bandmates to a sort of “analog AI” have only sunk the company’s standing further among the loudest of its fans online.T3 editor-in-chief Mat Gallagher’s feature mostly paraphrases Cole’s statements, and Fender did not immediately respond to a request for comment or clarification. But here are the relevant bits from the interview:Cole’s philosophy is that AI in music is nothing new. “I think AI has existed in music as long as there’s been recorded music,” he says. While the biggest barrier to playing guitar is the time it takes to learn the instrument, it’s the second barrier, writing songs, where he believes AI plays a part.“I actually believe cover music has been sort of analog AI for a long time,” says Cole. Those that don’t yet have the skills to write their own songs can play the songs written by their favourite artists instead. “I listened a lot to REM, U2, The Smiths and The Cure, and at some point I got sick of just listening to them. I wanted to play it, so I learned to play guitar.”Those taking their first steps into writing, according to Cole, can also lean on a second analogue form of AI: their band mates. You might just have a chorus or a riff to start with but then the drummer or bassist can add to it, and a song is born. AI can also play this role. “I actually think that we are in the brink of freeing up people to move beyond the same old covers and to really get into working like they do with their bands,” says Cole.Cole is trying to draw a comparison between a human “training” on a handful of cover songs and an AI ingesting enormous datasets of copyrighted music. He appears to be suggesting that, by learning to play other people’s songs, internalizing those influences, and then synthesizing them into something new, you are essentially doing the same thing as an AI. This is a woefully misguided take that says to me that Cole either doesn’t understand AI or doesn’t respect artists.For starters, scale matters. No person could possibly learn all of the songs used to train your average generative AI model, which, in the case of Suno, is suspected to be in the millions. Additionally, it dismisses the inherent humanity of the millions of tiny decisions, conscious or otherwise, that an artist makes during the songwriting process. Whether they’re driven by emotional response, reacting to a happy accident, or compensating for limitations, the artistic decisions made by a human are unique to them.This is fundamentally different from a model spitting out something based on a prompt and a network of data points. As Steve Onotera, better known as Samurai Guitarist, points out, a player’s physicality, or the tiny errors that every human is prone to, prevent them from replicating someone else’s work perfectly. That kind of serendipity can’t be replicated by an LLM.The same is true of bandmates. Humans who pull from their own unique sets of “training data,” life experiences, and physical skills or limitations are not the same as a chatbot. An AI doesn’t have taste or instincts in the way that your picky bassist who studied jazz composition in college does. If you told your drummer they were no different from an AI model, they’d rightfully be insulted.Later in the interview, Cole says: “I believe that AI is actually going to help create a whole new world of guitar players that use it. To help connect with other musicians, to be more productive. And across the chasm into becoming a student of songwriting to a master of songwriting.”Cole’s assertion that AI will somehow help people “across the chasm” to becoming master songwriters is also, frankly, ridiculous. Evidence is mounting that relying on AI tools is actually leading to deskilling. Using an AI to suggest rhymes or metaphors for pain isn’t the same as practicing songwriting and developing skills. The AI has never been left at the altar or sweated over the perfect pre-chorus transition. Repetition is the key. The adage is that you need to write 100 (or 1,000) (or 10,000) bad songs before you write one good one. That’s how you grow beyond tired tropes and learn to recognize when you’ve stumbled into something good.

items.titleZh: Fender 的 CEO 似乎认为你的乐队伙伴只是模拟 AI
items.descriptionZh:
Fender CEO爱德华·“巴德”·科尔在5月接受T3杂志采访时，为庆祝Telecaster吉他75周年发表了对AI与音乐的评论，当时并未引起太多关注。但近日这段言论在网络上重新传播，给公司本已糟糕的公众形象火上浇油——此前Fender向众多制琴师发送停止侵权函，声称拥有Stratocaster琴体形状的版权，激怒了整个吉他社区。一些有影响力的吉他YouTuber甚至表示，在这起争议之后不再购买Fender产品。而科尔那段将翻唱歌曲和乐队成员比作某种“模拟AI”的言论，进一步损害了公司在网上最活跃粉丝心中的地位。

科尔的核心观点是，音乐中的AI并非新鲜事物。“我认为只要有录音音乐存在，AI就存在于音乐中。”他指出，学习吉他最大的障碍是时间投入，而第二个障碍是写歌，AI正是能在写歌环节发挥作用。“我实际上认为翻唱音乐长期以来就是某种模拟AI。”那些还不具备原创能力的人可以演奏他们最喜欢的艺术家的歌曲。科尔本人就是通过这种方式学习吉他的：“我听了很多REM、U2、The Smiths和The Cure的歌，后来我厌倦了只是听，我想去演奏，所以我学会了吉他。”

科尔认为，初学写歌的人也可以依靠第二种“模拟AI”：他们的乐队伙伴。你可能只有一段副歌或一个即兴重复段，但鼓手或贝斯手可以加进来，一首歌就诞生了。AI也能扮演这个角色。“我确实觉得我们正处在这样一个临界点：人们将被解放出来，不再局限于老套的翻唱，而是真正像和乐队合作那样去创作。”

然而，评论者指出科尔的类比存在根本性缺陷。他将人类学习几首翻唱歌曲的过程与AI摄取海量受版权保护的数据集相提并论，暗示人类通过学弹别人的歌曲、吸收影响然后综合成新作品，本质上与AI做的事情一样。这种观点被批评为对AI缺乏理解或对艺术家缺乏尊重。

首先，规模完全不同。没有任何人能够学完一个生成式AI模型训练所用的全部歌曲——以Suno为例，其训练数据据推测可能达数百万首。其次，这种类比抹杀了艺术家在创作过程中做出的数百万个微小决定所蕴含的人性，这些决定无论是有意识还是无意识的，都源于情感反应、对偶然意外的应对或对自身局限的补偿，是独一无二的。这与AI根据提示和数据点网络生成输出的本质完全不同。正如网红吉他手Steve Onotera（网名Samurai Guitarist）指出的，演奏者的身体条件以及每个人都有的人为微小失误，使他们无法完美复制他人的作品，这种“意外之喜”是大型语言模型无法复制的。

乐队成员的情况也是如此。人类拥有各自独特的“训练数据”、生活经历和身体技能或局限，这与聊天机器人截然不同。AI不具备那种品味和直觉——比如你那位在大学学过爵士作曲的挑剔贝斯手所拥有的东西。如果你告诉鼓手他和AI模型没什么区别，他完全有理由感到被冒犯。

科尔还宣称“AI将帮助创造一个新世界的吉他手，帮助他们与其他音乐家联系，提高生产力，跨越从歌曲创作学徒到大师的鸿沟。”这一说法也被认为荒谬。越来越多的证据表明，依赖AI工具实际上会导致技能退化。用AI来建议押韵或比喻痛苦，与练习写歌、培养技能完全不同。AI从未经历过在人生关键时刻的失落，也不曾为完美的预副歌过渡而绞尽脑汁。重复是关键所在。俗话说，你需要写100首（或1000首，或10000首）烂歌才能写出一首好歌。这正是你摆脱陈词滥调、学会识别自己偶然写出好作品的方式。

总而言之，这场争议揭示了音乐行业对AI态度的深层分歧：Fender试图将AI描绘成创作民主化的工具，但批评者认为这种类比不仅贬低了人类创作的价值，也忽视了AI在规模、本质和创造力上的根本差异。对于Fender这样拥有深厚文化底蕴的品牌而言，在AI浪潮中如何平衡技术创新与尊重艺术传统，已成为一个亟待解决的核心问题。

history.descriptionZh:
由德国德累斯顿工业大学与英国曼彻斯特大学联合研究团队发表的技术论文《SpiNNaker2芯片：面向灵活可扩展类脑计算的多核平台》近日引发业界关注。该成果发表于半导体行业权威媒体Semiconductor Engineering，标志着类脑计算与深度学习两大技术路线之间正在出现实质性的融合节点。

**背景与上下文**

SpiNNaker系列芯片源自欧洲人脑计划（Human Brain Project），其核心理念是模拟生物神经网络的工作机制——通过大规模脉冲神经网络（Spiking Neural Network, SNN）实现事件驱动式计算。与传统的冯·诺依曼架构不同，SpiNNaker采用海量简单处理核心并行协作的方式，模仿大脑中神经元通过脉冲信号传递信息的模式。第一代SpiNNaker芯片于2011年问世，最初规划构建包含100万个ARM核的系统，但受限于功耗与制造工艺，实际规模与能效比均有提升空间。SpiNNaker2作为继承者，在架构设计上进行了根本性革新，其最突出的贡献在于：首次在硬件层面弥合了深度学习（深度神经网络）与神经形态计算之间的"鸿沟"。

**核心技术原理与创新**

SpiNNaker2的核心创新可归纳为三个层面。其一，"多核异构弹性计算"架构。芯片集成了数千个低功耗ARM处理器核心（Cortex-M系列架构），通过片上网络（Network-on-Chip）实现高带宽、低延迟的消息传递。与第一代相比，每个核心都增加了独立的动态电压与频率调节（DVFS）能力，这意味着不同核心可以根据任务负载实时调整功耗状态——类比生物大脑中神经元的兴奋与静息状态切换，能效较前代提升了一个数量级。

其二，"双重计算模式"融合。传统神经形态芯片（如IBM的TrueNorth）仅支持脉冲神经网络，而通用AI加速器（如GPU或NPU）侧重于连续数值的张量运算，两者互不兼容。SpiNNaker2在硬件层面同时支持两种模式：既能高效执行脉冲神经网络的稀疏、异步事件处理，也能完成传统深度网络所需的矩阵乘法与卷积运算。具体而言，芯片设计了可配置的乘累加单元，在脉冲模式下充当突触事件的积分器，在深度神经网络模式下则作为标准的MAC运算单元。这种双模设计允许开发者在一个平台上无缝切换或混用SNN与ANN模型。

其三，"片上学习"能力。SpiNNaker2内建了支持多种学习规则（包括脉冲时间依赖可塑性STDP、反向传播及在线梯度下降）的硬件逻辑，使芯片无需依赖外部主机即可完成模型训练与权重更新，这对于边缘场景中的持续学习至关重要。

**性能参数与对比分析**

论文报告了关键性能指标：在高性能模式下，SpiNNaker2可达到最高4.5 TOPS的算力。这一数字本身并非极致——相比之下，NVIDIA的嵌入式GPU Jetson Orin可提供约275 TOPS算力。但SpiNNaker2的价值不在于峰值算力的堆砌，而在于能效比与稀疏事件处理的效率。由于脉冲神经网络天然具备稀疏性和事件驱动特性，实际有效计算中无需像传统深度学习加速器那样激活所有乘法器；在典型SNN推理场景下，SpiNNaker2的每瓦特有效算力表现显著优于通用GPU方案。此外，芯片支持实时运行大规模脉冲神经网络仿真——这是GPU难以企及的——因为其片上通信网络严格设计为满足神经脉冲传播的时序要求，可对100万级神经元的网络进行实时模拟（相比第一代SpiNNaker的约10万级神经元，性能提升了约一个数量级）。多芯片可扩展性也是一大亮点：SpiNNaker2支持大规模互连，理论上可构建百亿神经元级别的超大规模系统，向全脑仿真目标迈进。

**技术影响与应用场景**

SpiNNaker2的出现对AI硬件生态具有多重意义。首先，它为研究社区提供了一个真正可编程的"类脑计算实验平台"——不同于功能固定的专用芯片，研究者可以在SpiNNaker2上试验新的神经元模型、连接拓扑和学习算法，这极大促进了计算神经科学的发展。其次，在产业应用层面，SpiNNaker2的"双模"能力使其成为边缘计算中兼顾深度神经网络与脉冲神经网络的理想选择：在功耗极度敏感的物联网设备、可穿戴健康监测终端中，SNN模式能以微瓦级功耗实现语音唤醒、异常事件检测；在需要更高精度的场景则切换至深度网络模式。机器人与无人机领域也受益明显：事件驱动的传感数据（如动态视觉传感器DVS输出）可直接与SNN计算对接，实现毫秒级响应。此外，德国德累斯顿工业大学与曼彻斯特大学联合组建的SpiNNcloud Systems公司已开始推进SpiNNaker2的商业化部署，拟构建以数千颗SpiNNaker2芯片组成的高密度计算集群，面向科研和工业用户提供类脑计算云服务。

总体而言，SpiNNaker2的突破在于证明了"神经形态"与"深度学习"这两个一度被视为此消彼长的技术方向可以在同一块硅片上共生共荣。它既是神经科学研究的先进工具，也为未来低功耗智能系统提供了全新的硬件基石。随着类脑芯片生态的逐步完善，我们有理由期待下一步将要出现的，是真正兼具大脑效率与深度学习能力的通用智能计算平台。

history.title: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
history.description: As AI systems outgrow copper interconnects, TSMC, Intel, Samsung Foundry, and GlobalFoundries are pursuing four distinctly different co-packaged optics strategies to bring optical connectivity closer to compute.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The requirements of AI clusters have made optical interconnections practical for scale-out connectivity, but as bandwidth requirements increase, optical connectivity is becoming viable for scale-up connections. As a result, the industry is moving optical interfaces closer to CPUs and GPUs, from the front-panel transceiver to the package itself through co-packaged optics (CPO), and eventually directly into the processor package.Optical connectivity has been used for decades, as electrical links cannot efficiently and reliably transmit data over long distances at high data transfer rates. However, the cost and complexity of optical components limited their use to long-reach connections.The importance of CPO is rising because electrical interconnects are no longer scaling as quickly as AI processors, and feeding thousands of accelerators within a data center requires an exponential increase in communication bandwidth. In a traditional optical networking architecture, the processor or switch ASIC communicates electrically with a pluggable optical transceiver located at the front panel of a server or switch. However, as signaling speeds climb to 200 Gb/s - 400 Gb/s per lane and beyond, transmitting electrical signals over long copper PCB traces on a motherboard becomes increasingly inefficient due to higher insertion loss, greater power consumption, and tighter signal integrity requirements.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While technically possible, it demands the use of better materials, retimers, complex compensation processing, and equalization circuitry, which increases the cost of server infrastructure and its power consumption. CPO moves optical engines next to the processor or switch ASIC to shorten the electrical path before signals are converted into light, which means lower power consumption per transmitted bit, increased bandwidth density, and predictable scalability. As a result, CPO is increasingly viewed as a necessary technology for next-generation AI infrastructure.Because AI is viewed as a major megatrend, CPO is set to become ubiquitous; there are dozens of companies working in the CPO ecosystem, including foundries, OSATs, optical I/O startups, laser manufacturers, fiber suppliers, packaging houses, and networking vendors. You may like Inside optical and the battle for scale Leading-edge foundry roadmaps for TSMC, Intel and Samsung — outlining the path to 1.4nm nodes and beyond Intel's EMIB packaging gains traction as chip designers look beyond TSMC's constrained CoWoS As there are so many vendors pursuing different goals with different strategies, for this story, we are going to limit ourselves only to companies that actually produce things and whose roadmaps reflect their technological capabilities. So far, only four foundries have publicly articulated meaningful CPO manufacturing strategies: Intel Foundry, GlobalFoundries, Samsung Foundry, and TSMC.The four companies each represent four different CPO strategies and have very distinct plans for the future, so their plans and capabilities may not be directly comparable. Nonetheless, reviewing their offerings gives us an idea about where the industry is going from the perspective of actual foundries.TSMC: COUPE for everythingTSMC has historically been absent from the optical connectivity market as a product supplier. However, having worked on silicon photonics for many years, it now has the broadest ecosystem and manufacturing roadmap with its Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE). (Image credit: TSMC)TSMC's silicon photonics technology roadmap currently has three stages that span from a 1.6 Tbps optical engine with conventional pluggable optics to a 12.8 Tbps optical engine located within a processor package. The COUPE roadmap is tightly coupled with the company's advanced packaging technologies and the evolution of the company's micro-ring modulators (MRMs) that modulate light and directly impact performance. As a result, several TSMC customers (e.g., Nvidia) plot their silicon photonics strategies around the evolution of COUPE.The first phase of the roadmap — called COUPE on PCB — relies on a COUPE that bonds a 65nm electronic integrated circuit (EIC) with a photonic integrated circuit (PIC) using the company's SoIC-X bonding technology. The initial implementation targets OSFP (Octal Small Form-factor Pluggable) optical modules and delivers 1.6 Tbps of bandwidth (2x the throughput of copper Ethernet solutions, along with 2x the power efficiency compared to copper). Therefore, the first-gen COUPE is out of the scope of this article. TSMC says the SoIC-X interface features very low impedance and enables lower power consumption at high signaling speeds. What to read next Trailing-edge foundry roadmaps for GlobalFoundries, UMC, and SMIC The custom AI ASIC state of play (May 2026) — Broadcom deals, Google TPUs, Meta MTIA & beyond Analyzing TSMC's fab expansion roadmap — multi-fab N2 ramp, CoWoS, SoIC, and uncorking bottlenecks The second generation — dubbed COUPE on substrate — marks TSMC's transition from conventional pluggable optics to co-packaged optics (CPO). In this stage, COUPE is integrated with the company's chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) advanced packaging technology and co-packaged with a network switch ASIC. This architecture enables motherboard-level optical interconnects with aggregate bandwidth up to 6.4 Tbps, 2x power efficiency, and 10x lower latency compared to existing pluggable solutions, which is fantastic for a variety of applications, such as NVLink, Ethernet, and InfiniBand switches.The third phase — called COUPE on interposer — pushes silicon photonics even closer to compute dies: a 12.8 Tbps optical engine is integrated directly into the processor package to enable ultimate bandwidth and scalability. Beyond doubling bandwidth again, the company expects the architecture to offer 5x power efficiency and 20x lower latency compared to pluggable solutions used today. That will make it particularly attractive for use by hyperscalers that build clusters consisting of thousands of accelerators. Unfortunately, TSMC characterizes this phase as exploratory and has not disclosed its commercialization timeline. Swipe to scroll horizontally TSMC COUPE's MRM Evolution Year 2026 2028 2029 2030 MRM / Lane Speed 200 Gb/s 200 Gb/s 200 Gb/s 400 Gb/s Bandwidth Density 0.5 Tbps/mm 1 Tbps/mm 2 Tbps/mm 4 Tbps/mm Wavelenght Single Single Multi Multi FAU Single-row FAU Dual-rou FAU Dual-rou FAU Dual-rou FAU The main agenda of COUPE is to move the optical engine as close to compute as possible. However, there is another dimension in TSMC's silicon photonics strategy: the evolution of the photonic devices themselves, the MRMs integrated into PICs. The company plans to bring the world's first 200 Gbps/lane (wavelength) micro-ring modulator into production in 2026 and then continue scaling the technology with 400 Gb/s MRMs, additional optical wavelengths, and denser fiber-array integration. This evolution is expected to increase COUPE’s bandwidth density from 0.5 Tb/s/mm in 2026 to 4 Tb/s/mm by 2030, providing an 8x improvement over four years.It is noteworthy that TSMC presents the MRM roadmap separately from the evolution of COUPE packaging, which suggests that advances in micro-ring modulators represent an independent technology roadmap for the photonic integrated circuit (PIC), rather than being tied to a specific packaging generation. This potentially means that future COUPE products could adopt newer generations of MRMs regardless of whether the optical engine is mounted on a PCB, package substrate, or silicon interposer, although the latter will probably deliver the greatest system-level benefits by minimizing the electrical distance between compute dies and optical interfaces.Intel: Optics for CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, and acceleratorsIntel has been shipping various products with optical interconnections for decades and even attached its silicon photonics solutions to Xeon and Xeon Phi processors in the mid-2010s. Today, Intel's public CPO roadmap is less explicit than TSMC's, but its direction is fairly clear: move optical I/O directly next to CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, and eventually other compute chiplets. Meanwhile, so far, Intel has not unveiled plans to use its CPO technology for switches. (Image credit: Intel)Intel's CPO strategy is largely focused on its Optical Compute Interconnect (OCI) chiplet, which is a self-contained optical I/O subsystem packing both EIC and PIC that can be co-packaged with any compute device using a PCIe interface to enable high-performance optical connectivity. Intel demonstrated the first OCI in 2024. That prototype implementation used 64 PCIe 5.0 lanes at 32 GT/s in each direction to connect to the host and provided 4 Tbps of bidirectional optical bandwidth over eight fiber pairs over a distance of up to 100 meters. Each fiber carried eight DWDM wavelengths spaced at 200 GHz, and every wavelength (lane) transported about 32 Gbps (8 FPs × 8 WLs × 32 Gbps = 2,048 Gbps in each direction). (Image credit: Intel)The 2024 OCI implementation is good for testing the technology, but with rather slow 32 Gbps lanes, it has not been adopted commercially. Meanwhile, this technology has already been proven and demonstrated. Intel is currently working on its next-generation OCI with 200G/lane PICs to support 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps applications, though it is unclear when it is set to be available, as Intel has not yet disclosed an equivalent to TSMC's MRM roadmap.It should be noted that future OCI implementations supporting bandwidth of 10s of terabits per second could interface with compute dies using next-generation PCIe 6.0 interfaces or even native die-to-die UCIe links when integrated into commercial products. Furthermore, Intel can naturally integrate OCI chiplets using its advanced packaging technologies to ensure high performance and low power. (Image credit: Intel)As noted above, Intel's focus with OCI has always been its integration with CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, accelerators, or other compute devices, but not necessarily switches. It remains to be seen whether Intel's next-generation AI hardware roadmap will include switching silicon, but for now, it does not seem that the company is targeting optical switches with its OCI chiplets. Since OCI is protocol-agnostic, limiting it to compute devices seems like an artificial limitation, though we have little indication about Intel's reasoning behind the decision.Samsung Foundry: Addressing everythingSamsung Foundry's silicon photonics strategy is arguably the most comprehensive among leading foundries. Unlike Intel, whose CPO roadmap is focused on its OCI chiplet for integration with compute devices, or TSMC, whose COUPE optical engine is another major ingredient of its foundry platform, Samsung intends to offer all types of optical connectivity devices, starting from pluggable transceivers in 2026, to switch CPO later on, and all the way to optical engines on the interposer of a processor package in 2030. Unfortunately, Samsung does not publicly provide a lot of information about its plans, so our main source of information will be SF's slide from a conference published by SemiVision. (Image credit: SemiVision)This year, Samsung Foundry intends to offer a merchant PIC platform that relies on an EIC and a PIC mounted side by side on a PCB for conventional pluggable optics. The PIC will support 100 Gbps-class optical interfaces using CWDM technology, which is good enough for traditional pluggable optical transceivers (though Samsung does not specify the exact implementation), so there's no indication of CPO here. (Image credit: Samsung)In 2027, Samsung Foundry intends to catch up with TSMC's first-gen COUPE and offer an optical engine that stacks an EIC on top of a PIC using thermo-compression bonding (TCB). Samsung expects energy efficiency of this generation to improve from approximately 10 pJ/bit for its initial PIC platform to 5 pJ/bit, though Samsung has said nothing about bandwidth or latency. Samsung's TCB-based OE seems to be an intermediate product between merchant PICs and true CPO, so it will generally address onboard optics and pluggable transceivers.By 2028, SF intends to move optical engines to the substrate of Ethernet or InfiniBand switch ASICs, which will be its first true CPO. The company intends to adopt hybrid copper bonding (HCB) with 10 µm pitches for its OEs to improve bandwidth density. Based on the slide from the roadmap, to address next-generation switches, Samsung is poised to increase optical lane speeds from 100 Gbps to 200 Gbps and ultimately 400 Gbps, although the company does not disclose when exactly each speed bin will be introduced (though it looks like 400 Gbps will come in 2029 – 2030) as well as the underlying modulator technology or other device-level details behind this scaling.In 2029, Samsung Foundry will finally integrate its optical engine on an interposer next to CPU/GPU/XPU or other compute device, which will reduce energy consumption to 2 pJ/bit while providing extremely high bandwidth. Samsung calls this 'CPO Turnkey,' which implies that such integration will require its own packaging technologies. The next step in Samsung's roadmap is called 'next-generation CPO Turnkey,' and it integrates virtually the entire optical subsystem — including lasers — alongside compute and memory, which will be its ultimate CPO offering expected by 2030 and onwards.While Samsung Foundry's ultimate goal to offer highly integrated turnkey CPO solutions is clear, the company also intends to offer two merchant platforms for pluggable optical transceivers, perhaps to de-risk development of its future products and to capitalize on the high demand for optical connectivity that exists today and will continue going forward.GlobalFoundries: A bespoke vendor-agnostic OCI-MSA CPO platformUnlike Intel Foundry, Samsung Foundry, and TSMC, GlobalFoundries does not produce or intend to produce AI processors, switch ASICs, or advanced packages. Instead, it aims to become a merchant co-packaged optics provider that will produce and sell bespoke CPO solutions that enable optical connectivity (including OCI MSA connectivity) for processors made by other chipmakers. (Image credit: GlobalFoundries)GF's silicon photonics effort dates back to the IBM Microelectronics acquisition in 2015, which brought IBM's silicon photonics technology and engineering teams into the company. Over the years, GlobalFoundries has expanded its silicon photonics capabilities into what eventually became the GF Fotonix platform and, more recently, the company acquired AMF and InfiniLink to further strengthen its production and design capabilities.The key element of GlobalFoundries' CPO strategy is its Silicon photonics Co-packaged Advanced Light Engine (SCALE) platform that combines photonic IP, advanced packaging technologies, and a reference optical engine architecture that includes EIC and PIC. Unlike Intel's OCI chiplet, SCALE allows GF's clients to customize optical engines in accordance with their needs and have them manufactured by GF.Under the program, GlobalFoundries manufactures the PIC and EIC using its own process technologies and then packages them into an OCI MSA-compliant optical engine using its methods. If the EIC requires a leading-edge node that GF does not have, it could instead be fabricated by another foundry and then integrated by GF. Customers then co-package the optical engine alongside their own switch ASICs or AI accelerators.For now, SCALE supports both CWDM and DWDM transmission using qualified 50 Gbps and 100 Gbps MRMs, integrated photodiodes, and coupled-ring resonators. The platform has demonstrated bidirectional operation with up to 16 DWDM lanes per fiber, which theoretically opens doors to optical links with up to 1.6 Tb/s of bandwidth per direction. On the integration side of things, it supports advanced 2.5D and 3D integration using TSVs and copper bonding with pitches ranging from 110 µm to below 45 µm, which is good enough for integration using CoWoS-S and CoWoS-L technologies.Just like Intel with its OCI, GlobalFoundries does not necessarily tie its SCALE CPO customers to its silicon or packaging technologies. Furthermore, the company allows its clients to customize their optical engines while retaining compatibility with the OCI-MSA requirements.The future of CPO Co-packaged optics (CPO) is set to become a key technology for next-generation AI infrastructure as conventional electrical interconnects struggle to keep pace with the bandwidth demands of rapidly developing AI processors.Among foundries, TSMC, Intel, Samsung Foundry, and GlobalFoundries have each developed distinct CPO strategies that range from merchant optical engines to optical I/O chiplets and vertically integrated CPO platforms.Given the different capabilities of the contract chipmakers, their roadmaps differ significantly in both scope and implementation, with some companies trying to lock in customers with a proprietary platform and others offering different degrees of freedom.However, they all share the same objective: move optical interfaces progressively closer to compute dies to reduce power consumption, increase bandwidth density, and lower latency for the next generation of AI systems that will require considerably more bandwidth than today's clusters.

history.titleZh: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
history.descriptionZh:
随着AI集群规模不断扩大，传统电互连已难以满足海量加速器之间爆炸式增长的通信带宽需求。虽然光互连已在长距离传输中应用数十年，但过去由于成本和复杂度较高，仅用于远距离连接。如今，光互连正从服务器前面板的可插拔光模块向芯片封装内部迁移，即“共封装光学”（Co-Packaged Optics, CPO）技术——将光引擎移至处理器或交换ASIC的旁边，在信号转换为光之前大幅缩短电学传输路径。这样做不仅能降低每比特传输功耗，还能提高带宽密度并实现可预测的扩展性，因此被视为下一代AI基础设施的关键技术。

在CPO生态系统中，目前只有四家晶圆代工厂公开了明确的制造路线图：台积电、英特尔、三星代工和格芯（GlobalFoundries）。它们各自代表四种不同的技术路径，未来发展策略与能力各具特色。

**台积电：COUPE路线图**

台积电通过其“紧凑型通用光子引擎”（COUPE）平台制定了三阶段硅光发展计划，并与自有先进封装技术和微环调制器（MRM）的演进深度绑定。第一阶段“COUPE on PCB”采用65nm电子IC（EIC）与光子IC（PIC）通过SoIC-X键合技术堆叠，用于OSFP光模块，提供1.6Tbps带宽，功率效率为铜缆的两倍，但不属于CPO范畴。第二阶段“COUPE on substrate”标志着向共封装光学过渡，光引擎集成到CoWoS先进封装中，与网络交换ASIC共封装，可实现6.4Tbps聚合带宽、2倍功率效率以及相比可插拔方案低10倍的延迟，适用于NVLink、以太网和InfiniBand交换机。第三阶段“COUPE on interposer”则是直接把12.8Tbps光引擎集成进处理器封装内，预期可提供5倍功率效率和20倍延迟改善，非常适合构建数千个加速器的超大规模集群，但该阶段目前仍处于探索期，商业化时间未定。

台积电另一条独立的技术演进路线是微环调制器。公司计划在2026年推出业界首个200Gbps/波长的微环调制器，后续进一步提升至400Gb/s，并引入多波长支持和更密集的光纤阵列。这将使COUPE的带宽密度从2026年的0.5Tbps/mm提升至2030年的4Tbps/mm，四年内提升8倍。值得注意的是，MRM路线图与COUPE封装阶段分开演进，意味着未来无论光引擎位于PCB、基板还是硅中介层上，都可以采用更新的调制器技术，从而获得系统级性能提升。

**英特尔：面向计算设备的光学互连小芯片**

英特尔长期深耕光互连产品，早在2010年代中期就将硅光方案与Xeon处理器结合。其CPO战略的核心是“光学计算互连”（OCI）小芯片——一个完整的、同时包含EIC和PIC的光I/O子系统，可通过PCIe接口与任意计算设备共封装。2024年展示的OCI原型采用双向各64条PCIe 5.0通道（每通道32GT/s），通过8对光纤提供4Tbps双向光带宽，每根光纤承载8个间隔200GHz的DWDM波长，每个波长速率约32Gbps，传输距离达100米。不过该原型通道速率偏低（32Gbps），尚未商业化。目前英特尔正在开发采用200G/通道PIC的下一代OCI，支持800Gbps和1.6Tbps应用，但时间表未公布。未来OCI有望通过PCIe 6.0或UCIe原生芯粒互连接口与计算die连接，支持数十Tbps级别带宽。与台积电不同，英特尔当前OCI定位明确指向CPU、GPU、DPU和加速器，而非交换芯片；由于OCI协议无关，这一限制更多是策略选择而非技术必然。

**三星代工：从可插拔到Turnkey全覆盖**

三星代工的硅光路线图在前沿代工厂中覆盖最广，从2026年的可插拔方案逐步走向2030年的高度集成封装。2026年，三星计划提供采用EIC和PIC并列放置在PCB上的商用PIC平台，支持100Gbps级CWDM光接口，应用于传统可插拔光模块。2027年，采用热压键合（TCB）将EIC堆叠在PIC上方，能效从约10pJ/bit提升至5pJ/bit，这属于板载光学而非真正的CPO。到2028年，三星将把光引擎转移至以太网或InfiniBand交换ASIC的封装基板上，这是其第一款真正意义上的CPO产品，采用混合铜键合（HCB）技术，间距10微米，通道速率计划从100Gbps逐步提升至400Gbps（后者预计在2029至2030年之间）。2029年，光引擎将集成到中介层上，与CPU/GPU/XPU相邻，能效降至2pJ/bit，带宽极高，三星称其为“CPO Turnkey”。而2030年及以后的“下一代CPO Turnkey”将把包括激光器在内的几乎整个光学子系统与计算和内存一同封装，达到终极集成度。此外，三星还会提供两个商用可插拔方案平台，既为了增加收入，也为了降低未来CPO开发风险。

**GlobalFoundries：定制化、厂商中立的SCALE平台**

与前三家不同，格芯不生产AI处理器或交换ASIC，而是定位为独立CPO供应商，为其他芯片厂商制造定制光引擎。其硅光技术源自2015年收购IBM微电子业务，经过多年扩展形成GF Fotonix平台，近期又并购了AMF和InfiniLink以强化设计与生产。格芯CPO战略的核心是“SCALE”平台（Silicon photonics Co-packaged Advanced Light Engine），整合了光子IP、先进封装技术和包含EIC/PIC的参考光引擎架构。客户可根据需求定制光引擎，并交由格芯制造；即使客户需要更先进的EIC节点，格芯也可将其外包给其他代工厂再集成。SCALE平台目前支持CWDM和DWDM传输，采用经过验证的50Gbps/100Gbps微环调制器、集成光电探测器和耦合环形谐振器，已演示在单根光纤上支持多达16个DWDM波长，理论可实现每方向最高1.6Tbps光链路。集成方面支持TSV和铜键合，间距从110微米到低于45微米，可兼容CoWoS-S和CoWoS-L等封装技术。同时格芯不强制绑定自有硅工艺或封装路线，允许客户在符合OCI MSA标准的前提下灵活定制。

总的来看，CPO正在成为下一代AI基础设施不可或缺的支撑技术。台积电、英特尔、三星代工和格芯虽路径各异——有的以专有平台锁定客户，有的提供更大自由度——但目标一致：将光学接口不断推向计算die附近，以降低功耗、提升带宽密度并减少延迟，满足未来AI系统远高于当前集群的通信要求。

history.title: GPU prices keep surging in 2026 — Lack of sale discounts and rising VRAM costs keep current-gen prices sky-high
history.description: AI, tariffs, and greed have put pressure on PC builders wanting a new GPU. Can you still get a cheap GPU?
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter We all know the current state of pricing for PC components is through the roof. Looking back, we have the hindsight to see what the prices were a year or two ago, and be thankful that we bought something when it was cheaper or on a really good sale. But for those who didn’t upgrade back then, what does the future look like if you want to upgrade your graphics card?Currently, we have access to the 50-series range of graphics cards from Nvidia, and the 90-series from AMD, with a couple of entries from Intel. These cards were primarily released in January 2025, with different graphics card SKUs released throughout the year. We’re now more than halfway through 2026, with the rumored release of the next generation of graphics cards not arriving until late 2027, or even 2028, so we’re looking at at least a year before we see any hint of a new GPU release.Why the delay or extended release cadence? Well, the simple answer is the costs. Just one aspect of the increased costs incurred with any new graphics card release will be the high-speed memory used, and, in the GPU's case, the amount of VRAM. Prices have become exponentially more expensive due to the AI crunch, so adding more memory to a GPU is going to not only increase the production costs of any new graphics card direct from Nvidia or AMD, but also boost the expenses that AIB board partners have to incur to offer the partner GPUs. These manufacturing cost rises will, of course, be passed on to us poor consumers. There might even be reductions in the amount of onboard VRAM for different card SKUs; we will have to wait to find out.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: There are no stock issues with picking up a new GPU; the main issue is just the cost. I keep track of all the current graphics card prices twice weekly in our GPU Price Index, and have seen the prices creep up steadily since release, especially with the higher-end and more popular GPUs, or those deemed the best performance per dollar.Here are two tables that show the initial MSRP launch prices of Nvidia’s 50-series and AMD’s 90-series graphics cards, along with the current price and the lowest prices that we’ve seen for each card. This generation of cards was released with a higher MSRP, and many GPUs released were well above the announced MSRP prices set by Nvidia and AMD, garnering a lot of criticism from both the press and consumers. What’s also been highly noticeable this generation is the lack of notable below-MSRP discounts in major sales events such as Black Friday or Prime Day. You may like MSI and Colorful raise Nvidia RTX 50-series prices in China by up to 59% across the entire lineup GPU price tracking 2026: Lowest price on every graphics card from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel today The rise of local agentic computing faces a brutal reality: rising DRAM prices Swipe to scroll horizontally GPU Model Best US Price Lowest-Ever U.S. Price MSRP Launch Price GeForce RTX 5090 $4,288 $1,999 $1,999 GeForce RTX 5080 $1,256 $929 $999 GeForce RTX 5070 Ti $949 $729 $749 GeForce RTX 5070 $629 $479 $549 GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16GB $569 $379 $429 GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB $429 $319 $379 GeForce RTX 5060 $339 $279 $299 GeForce RTX 5050 $289 $229 $249 Swipe to scroll horizontally GPU Model Best US Price Lowest-Ever U.S. Price MSRP Launch Price Radeon RX 9070 XT $719 $599 $599 Radeon RX 9070 $639 $494 $549 Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB $449 $349 $349 Radeon RX 9060 XT 8GB $359 $259 $299 We can see that, in general, the lowest-ever prices seen are barely below the launch MSRP prices, if at all. With cards such as Nvidia’s flagship GeForce RTX 5090 never dropping below its initial release price. In the case of the RTX 5090, the price of the top-tier GPU that features 32GB of precious VRAM has only ever increased, rising from $1,999 to $4,288, a staggering $2,289 (114.5%) difference.As I see the cheapest models sell out while I’m checking on the weekly prices, the cost of the GPU just keeps climbing a little higher every time. Although the RTX 5090 is the most extreme example of GPU inflation, it is unfortunately not alone.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)AMD’s Radeon RX 9070 XT, which many feel to be the value champion for high-end GPUs, competes against Nvidia RTX 5070 Ti, but for several hundred dollars less. Up until very recently, the 9070 XT held a steady $699 retail price, but as of writing, the price has jumped to $719, a $120 hike from the $599 launch MSRP price, a 20% increase. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)To help in your decision of what card you want to buy, consider what features the card offers and what you will make use of. Is ray-tracing important to you? Does frame gen technology interest you? Are the video encoders and codecs for streaming or video capture better for your associated software? Do your research; don’t just look at graphs with FPS numbers. Think about what is going to give you the most overall benefit.Other things to also consider are the differences in the supporting software, such as FSR and DLSS, with Nvidia slightly ahead for the most part for the latest technology, but with the caveat that they are also more expensive. AMD cards this generation have offered more VRAM on lower-end GPU SKUs, which can be an important feature for gamers playing on higher-resolution monitors with game settings dialed up.If you want a graphics card now, you don’t have much choice but to grab what you can at the lowest price that’s available to you at the moment. Holding out for the next generation of GPUs often isn’t going to save you any money; as with all technology, obsolescence is a fact of life.We have to wait for the definitive specifications to be announced for the new GPU lineups, and until then, everything is educated guesswork and speculation. Whether reductions in onboard VRAM allocations take place, GPU die size shrinks, or core counts multiply, all wait to be seen. Whatever happens, though, one thing is guaranteed, and that is that the new lineup will be more expensive than this generation; we just don’t know yet by how much.Finding a massive discount on a graphics card in the current economic climate is going to be limited to stores making pricing mistakes or some serious combo bundle deals from retailers. Seeing how even the Nvidia 40-series and AMD 70-series GPUs have held value and not greatly depreciated is an indication that the current generation of cards is not going to see massive discounts closer to the launch of the next generation. We hold out hope that we may see some discounts in the next Black Friday sales, but I wouldn’t count on seeing anything truly jaw-dropping, although I do hope to be proven wrong.
history.author: Stewart Bendle
history.titleZh: GPU价格在2026年持续飙升——缺乏促销折扣和显存成本上涨使当前世代价格居高不下
history.descriptionZh:
PC显卡市场正经历前所未有的价格暴涨，这已成为当前硬件领域最受关注的话题。回顾一两年前的价格，如今再想升级显卡的消费者无疑会感到沉重的经济压力。目前市场上可供选择的主要是英伟达（Nvidia）的RTX 50系列和AMD的RX 90系列显卡，另有英特尔（Intel）的几款产品，这些显卡大多在2025年1月发布，不同型号在此后陆续上市。然而，当前时间已进入2026年年中，下一代显卡据传要到2027年底甚至2028年才会亮相，这意味着玩家至少还要等待一年以上才有可能看到新GPU的影子。

这一漫长的产品周期背后，核心原因归结为一个字：成本。任何新显卡的推出都伴随着高昂的制造成本，而其中最具代表性的便是高速显存（VRAM）的支出。由于人工智能（AI）热潮引发的算力竞赛，显存颗粒的价格呈指数级上涨。这意味着无论是英伟达还是AMD直接推出的公版显卡，还是AIB合作伙伴（如华硕、微星、技嘉等）推出的非公版产品，其生产成本都将大幅抬升——更多的显存意味着更高的物料成本，而这些最终都会转嫁给消费者。更令人担忧的是，为了控制成本，未来不同型号的显卡甚至可能在板载显存容量上做出缩减，具体细节仍需拭目以待。

与往年不同，目前购买新显卡已不存在缺货问题，真正的障碍纯粹是价格。Tom's Hardware的GPU价格指数追踪显示，自发布以来，各款显卡的价格持续稳步攀升，尤其是高端型号和性价比口碑较好的热门产品。从两张价格对比表中可以清晰看到这一趋势的严峻程度。英伟达RTX 50系列方面，旗舰RTX 5090的官方建议零售价（MSRP）为1,999美元，历史最低价也从未跌破此价位，但当前最佳购买价已飙升至4,288美元，涨幅高达2,289美元，即114.5%。RTX 5080从999美元的MSRP涨至1,256美元，最低曾降至929美元；RTX 5070 Ti从749美元涨至949美元；RTX 5070从549美元涨至629美元；RTX 5060 Ti 16GB从429美元涨至569美元；RTX 5060 Ti 8GB从379美元涨至429美元；RTX 5060从299美元涨至339美元；RTX 5050从249美元涨至289美元。AMD RX 90系列同样不容乐观，被许多玩家视为高端性价比之王的RX 9070 XT，MSRP为599美元，此前一直稳定在699美元零售价，而截至本文撰写时已跳涨至719美元，较首发价高出120美元，涨幅达20%。RX 9070从549美元涨至639美元；RX 9060 XT 16GB从349美元涨至449美元；RX 9060 XT 8GB从299美元涨至359美元。

纵观整体数据，各款显卡的历史最低价几乎都难以跌破首发MSRP，甚至许多型号从未低于发布价格。这一代显卡在发布之初就定下了较高的MSRP，而实际上市价格更是普遍远超官方定价，引发了媒体和消费者的广泛批评。尤为值得注意的是，即便是黑色星期五或Prime Day这类传统的大型促销活动，也鲜见低于MSRP的大幅折扣——这在过去几代产品中几乎不可想象。

RTX 5090作为搭载32GB珍贵显存的顶级旗舰，是GPU通胀最极端的案例，但绝非孤例。从作者追踪每周价格的经历来看，最便宜的型号总是迅速售罄，而剩余显卡的价格则每次都在小幅攀升。这种"越等越贵"的态势让持币观望的消费者陷入两难。

在选购建议方面，专家提醒消费者不应仅仅盯着帧率（FPS）数字对比图，而应综合考虑显卡的实际功能特性：光线追踪性能是否符合你的需求？帧生成技术（Frame Generation）是否吸引你？视频编码器和编解码器是否更适合你使用的流媒体或录制软件？同时，配套软件生态的差异也值得关注——AMD的FSR与Nvidia的DLSS各有优劣，英伟达在最新技术上总体略微领先，但价格也更高昂；AMD这一代在中低端型号上提供了更大的显存容量，这对于在高分辨率显示器上开启高画质设置的玩家来说是一个重要考量因素。

对于当下需要升级显卡的消费者，现实的选择并不多：只能以当前能找到的最低价格尽快入手。等待下一代产品往往并不能省钱——正如所有科技产品一样，迭代与淘汰是不可避免的宿命。在下一代GPU的最终规格公布之前，一切关于显存容量调整、芯片制程缩减或核心数量增加的说法都只是基于现有信息的合理推测。但有一件事是确定的：下一代显卡阵容必将比当前这一代更加昂贵，只是我们尚不清楚贵多少而已。

在当前的经济环境下，想要找到大幅折扣的显卡，恐怕只能寄望于零售商的定价失误或罕见的捆绑促销套餐。一个值得注意的信号是，就连英伟达40系列和AMD 70系列的上一代产品至今仍保持着较好的保值率，没有出现大幅贬值，这表明当前这一代显卡在下一代发布前夕也不太可能迎来大规模降价。作者表示，尽管希望在下一个黑色星期五能看到一些真正令人心动的优惠，但从目前的市场态势来看，恐怕不宜抱有过高的期待。

history.content: Chinese tech giant Alibaba released what it says is its largest and “most capable AI model to date,” claiming performance rivaling the best systems from US frontier labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as domestic rivals like Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3. Alibaba said it was making the model, Qwen3.8-Max, widely available to users in a blog post published on Monday. The release had been expected after the company previewed the model last month, when it claimed it was “second only to Fable 5,” Anthropic’s flagship.The open release of another highly capable Chinese AI model adds to sky-high tensions along multiple fronts in Silicon Valley and Washington over how to safely manage AI systems and retain the US’ technological edge over China.Results from Alibaba’s own testing shared on Monday suggests it’s as powerful as claimed, as does its ranking on crowdsourced model-comparison platform Arena.AI. Alibaba’s own testing shows the model’s performance to broadly match — and sometimes exceed — that of Fable 5 on benchmark tests. On the Arena text model leaderboard, Qwen3.8-Max trails only Fable 5 and three models in Anthropic’s Opus family. For frontend coding, it is beaten only by two Claude Opus models and Kimi K3, and for visual analysis, only Fable 5 trounces it.Alibaba says Qwen3.8-Max has 2.4 trillion parameters, a numerical measure of the settings a model learns during training that it uses to process data, recognize patterns, and undertake various tasks. While parameter counts are widely used as a shorthand for model performance, a bigger number does not always mean better. Moonshot’s Kimi K3 model has 2.8 trillion parameters, but most top American labs keep figures private, and neither OpenAI nor Anthropic disclose exact counts for their top systems.The Chinese company said it will release the weights for Qwen3.8-Max next week. Weights are the adjustable numerical values of an AI that determine how it processes information. Open-weight systems, while more restrictive than traditional open-source software, give developers far more control than they have over proprietary products from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Qwen3.8-Max marks a return to open-weight releases for Alibaba after the company briefly pivoted towards proprietary releases for its more advanced models earlier this year.Open-weight releases have become a growing point of differentiation for China’s AI industry, where they have become the norm. Moonshot released Kimi K3’s last week and many other top AI models are also open-weight. Beijing has championed the strategy as a means of growing China’s influence in global AI governance and encouraging widespread adoption of domestic tech champions.Alibaba’s release intensifies competition with China, whose firms appear to be rapidly narrowing the gap with US companies and have increased the tempo of releases in recent weeks. Qwen3.8-Max closely follows the release of Kimi K3, viewed as another challenge to American AI dominance, and both ByteDance and MiniMax released capable new video generation models on Friday.Openness has also proved to be a divisive issue. Amid reports of potential crackdown on open tools in the wake of the Chinese releases, the US industry has largely rallied around preserving access to open-weight models, both as a safety necessity and as means of preserving competition. That debate comes as closed-model providers, notably OpenAI and Anthropic, face increasing scrutiny after revealing a slew of cyberattacks unknowingly perpetrated by their own escaped AI agents. Incident reports from one victim suggest the restrictive safety rails intended to stop nefarious use of AI models also limits their use as defensive tools.
